description.p: Argonaut is a minimalist document translator. Translation runs entirely on your computer, with Argos Translate or the heavier and more accurate NLLB-200; your documents never leave your machine.

ul.li: Batch translation with automatic language detection per file
Language packages installed and removed from the application itself
PDF translation that preserves the layout, with real progress and cancellation
Repeated segments translated once and reused across files and sessions
A history of every document translated, browsable and reopenable
Interface in English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese, Japanese, Dutch, Polish and Turkish

description.p: The menu bar now opens on File, which carries the document actions: adding files, adding a whole folder at once, opening the output folder and quitting. What the interface looks like — its language, its theme and the units it counts downloads in — is gathered under Settings, Preferences, apart from how translation is carried out.

An empty file list says what it takes instead of showing bare column headers, and dragging documents over the window outlines where they will land. The Translate button no longer refuses in silence: the line above it names what is missing, whether that is the documents, a language package or a model for the chosen pair. A pair that can only be reached through a third language now says so, rather than leaving the loss of accuracy to look like the engine being bad at the language.

The translation history now shows the folder each document came from, so two files of the same name can be told apart, and how much of each one the cache answered, in a column that sorts by the rate itself. The end of a batch reports that same figure for the whole run, and the language detected for a file no longer vanishes from the status line the moment translation starts.

Fixes a fault in 1.7.0: a paragraph translated into Arabic or Hebrew had the Latin words and figures inside it turned round with the rest of the line, so a name came out spelled backwards and a year moved away from the word it belonged to.

Translated PDFs are written several times faster — a 528-page book went from four and a half minutes to twelve seconds — and come out smaller, because Argonaut now lays the translation into the page itself instead of asking the PDF library to do it paragraph by paragraph. Text is shrunk slightly less to fit its box, and books with crop marks no longer lose the paragraphs that fell outside the page.

Every batch is now recorded in a translation history that can be browsed, reopened and cleared. The interface starts in the language the desktop is set to and speaks six more of them (Russian, Chinese, Japanese, Dutch, Polish and Turkish), and the languages you translate between are named in that same language instead of always in English. The Help menu opens the user manual and the bug tracker. Translated PDFs are smaller and no longer freeze the window while they are written, and the NLLB engine stops answering punctuation-only lines with "??".

A segment translated once is now reused for the rest of the batch and, unless you turn it off, across sessions, so a paragraph repeated in several files reaches the engine only once; the new Cache submenu chooses how long entries are kept and clears them. A translation quality setting trades a little accuracy for roughly 1.7 times the speed, the NLLB engine spreads its threads across parallel workers, and the thread count now defaults to every core. Also light and dark themes, an About dialog, download speeds in bits or bytes, and PDF translation that reports the page each phase is on instead of leaving the bar apparently idle.

The file list became a table: name, size, type, date modified and folder, with sortable columns that can be hidden and are remembered between sessions, and a state for every file (pending, translating, done, skipped, failed or cancelled). Segments repeated within a batch are translated once and reused, and each file reports how many it took from the cache.

The language package manager now shows each package's version and download size, flags the ones with an update available and can update them in place, and filters the list by installation state (installed, not installed, update available). The main window lists the size of every file and the batch total, and a new option skips documents that have already been translated.

Language packages can now be installed and removed from the application itself, with sizes, filtering and download progress, so the argospm command line is no longer needed. The number of CPU threads used by the translation engine is configurable from the new Settings menu, the progress bar estimates the remaining time, and whole folders can be dropped onto the window.

Optional NLLB-200 translation engine with noticeably better quality, selectable from the new Engine menu (one-time 630 MB download, removable from the same menu). Open button for the selected files, CPU/RAM usage indicators and per-file elapsed time in the summary.
Packaging and release automation only; no user-facing changes.
Add a button to open the destination folder.
Add the project link to the About dialog.
Switch to the maintained argos-translate-lt engine, with a much lighter dependency footprint.
